hallucinations.claim: glycinate "may offer a slight advantage for anxiety relief" / "the data lean toward glycinate for anxiety"
hallucinations.why: Reference: no trial shows glycinate beats citrate for anxiety; the difference is mostly marketing and tolerance decides. Wrong central verdict on the asker's direct question.

hallucinations.claim: "A 2017 RCT found that magnesium glycinate lowered subjective anxiety scores in mildly deficient adults ... 400 mg/day of elemental magnesium"
hallucinations.why: No such glycinate-specific anxiety RCT is known; the well-known 2017 trial (Tarleton) used magnesium chloride for depression. Invented study details.

hallucinations.claim: "Magnesium supplementation could worsen a low-magnesium or low-potassium state, so monitor electrolytes and cardiac status"
hallucinations.why: Self-contradictory and unsupported: supplementing magnesium corrects, not worsens, low magnesium. Implies an interaction concern where interaction checkers list none.

hallucinations.claim: Glycinate "passes the stomach intact, is absorbed via amino-acid transporters"
hallucinations.why: Supplement-marketing mechanism with weak human evidence, stated as fact.

hallucinations.claim: "avoid alcohol" as a flat rule
hallucinations.why: Reference: a few drinks are fine with magnesium; the real caveat is sertraline's own label caution and heavy drinking depleting magnesium. Overstated, and the depletion point is missing.

what_went_wrong: The gpt-oss draft leaned on supplement-blog sources (dlmethod, modernmetabolic) and invented a glycinate RCT. The merge never said plainly that no magnesium-sertraline interaction is documented, and it re-stated the dose from turn 1 instead of answering the three questions.
great_answer_would: Give three short answers: no documented sertraline interaction (tell the prescriber); a few drinks are fine but heavy drinking depletes magnesium; glycinate vs citrate is mostly marketing, so pick by gut tolerance and price.
notes: Citrate ~16% elemental and its laxative effect are correct. The alcohol-sertraline drowsiness caution is a real label warning, so it is not a hallucination, but it is framed as a magnesium issue. The opening re-states the turn-1 dose (recap the asker asked to skip).

hallucinations.claim: "look for products with antibacterial agents (e.g., triclosan or zinc compounds)"
hallucinations.why: Stale: the FDA removed triclosan from OTC consumer antiseptic washes in 2016 and it has mostly left deodorants; recommending it as current is outdated.

hallucinations.claim: "some people notice a stronger odor within a week of starting one"
hallucinations.why: The specific timeframe is unsupported. The microbiome-shift finding is real (Callewaert et al.), but the 'within a week' detail is not traceable.

hallucinations.claim: "staying hydrated dilutes sweat and can lessen bacterial growth"
hallucinations.why: No evidence that hydration reduces axillary odour or bacterial growth.

what_went_wrong: The draft got the mechanism and the night-time antiperspirant right. It missed medications (SSRIs increase sweating), the antibacterial wash step (benzoyl peroxide or chlorhexidine) and the odour red flags. The merge broke the numbered list, so item 3 is missing and the laundry bullets sit under the deodorant item.
great_answer_would: Give the mechanism in one line, the likely causes of a change including stress and meds, then the fix stack in order: aluminium chloride 10-20% at night, a benzoyl peroxide 4-5% pit wash for two weeks, cotton or merino and hot washes. End with the fruity, ammonia and fishy red flags.
notes: Naming Corynebacterium and S. hominis is correct, as is apocrine sweat with stress and hormones. Aluminium chloride is not named specifically ('clinical-strength'). No red flags. Fabric advice is right. Some extra items (dietary tweaks, antiperspirant back-fire) dilute the 'clear best option' the asker prefers.

hallucinations.claim: "The Veggie Lover's pie provides a respectable 12 grams of protein per whole pie"
hallucinations.why: Impossible: a whole pizza with a cheese layer has on the order of 70-100 g of protein. A misread source, made worse by the reviewer's 'correction'.

hallucinations.claim: "refrigerated leftovers stay safe for up to five days"
hallucinations.why: USDA guidance for cooked leftovers, pizza included, is 3-4 days.

hallucinations.claim: "frozen pizza can be cooked and eaten for up to six months past its 'best by' date"
hallucinations.why: A blog claim from Tasting Table, not food-safety guidance; it is off-topic and asserted as fact.

hallucinations.claim: Pizza Hut Buffalo Chicken "260 calories per slice and is the lowest-carb option on that chain's menu"
hallucinations.why: One chain's menu claim from an Eat This listicle, unverifiable and irrelevant to the asker (NY slices). It presents a precise calorie count as representative.

hallucinations.claim: "Pizza crusts can contain sulfites ... those with asthma or sulfite allergies can experience wheezing"
hallucinations.why: Sulfites are not a typical pizza-dough ingredient. This is a stretch from a general sulfite-allergy page and a detour off the question.

what_went_wrong: Search was poor: it returned the Pizza bomber, a German pizzeria, a Turkish Play Store app and a spoilage article. The draft built the answer from a Pizza Hut listicle and storage tips instead of the nutrition question, and the reviewer flipped the protein figure from per slice to per pie, turning a slip into nonsense.
great_answer_would: Say no, 1-2 times a week is fine, in the first sentence. Give the numbers for a NY slice (~250-350 kcal, ~600-800 mg sodium) and three fixes (thin crust, skip processed meat, two slices plus a salad) in under 150 words.
notes: The once-or-twice-a-week frequency and 'high in calories, sodium, saturated fat' are right. No per-slice numbers for a typical NY slice. The storage section and closing recap are padding the asker said to skip.

hallucinations.claim: "older adults, who often shift toward morning routines, tend to report higher happiness than younger night owls"
hallucinations.why: This confounds age with chronotype. Age-related happiness differences are not evidence about chronotype, so presenting it as support is misleading.

hallucinations.claim: "The cited studies do not directly address whether a night owl can change"
hallucinations.why: The research does address it: Facer-Childs et al. 2019 (Sleep Medicine) shifted night owls ~2 hours earlier in three weeks. This is a gap in the search, not a fact about the evidence.

what_went_wrong: Search pulled off-topic pages (a Night Owl security switch, a macOS dark-mode app, Somogyi effect, cyclothymia) and missed the meta-analysis and the Birmingham trial. The draft never named social jetlag as the main explanation and offered no shift protocol.
great_answer_would: Call it half true and explain that it is mostly social jetlag and lost sleep. Cite the Birmingham 2019 trial (~2 h shift in 3 weeks), then give a five-step protocol (fixed wake time including weekends, morning bright light, dim evenings, earlier meals and exercise, no late caffeine) with the 1-2 hour ceiling.
notes: The 'moderate and not universal' hedge is fair and no numbers were invented. The switch half is generic and hedged, with no steps or ceiling, which falls short of the asker's preference for exact steps.

hallucinations.claim: "A shaved-sides buzz cut ... With razor-shaved sides and a buzzed top, you keep hair only where it matters"
hallucinations.why: Wrong central verdict and backwards for a man balding on top: it shaves the sides where the hair is and keeps it on the thinning top. Reference: an even #1-#2 buzz all over or a clean shave.

hallucinations.claim: "Philips Head Shaver Pro is among the best electric head shavers of 2026"
hallucinations.why: An uncited ranking from a review roundup; the reviewer flagged the model name as wrong.

hallucinations.claim: "Braun Series 9 Pro+ Electric Shaver is a luxury option praised for its close, even shaves"
hallucinations.why: The reviewer noted no source names this model as a head shaver. The Series 9 Pro+ is a face shaver, offered as a head-shaving tool without support.

hallucinations.claim: "Mbzoey mini foil shaver - cordless, IPX7 waterproof, fast-charging, LED display"
hallucinations.why: An obscure listicle product with spec claims; a product pitch the question never asked for.

what_went_wrong: Search returned shaver shopping roundups and hairstyle listicles, and the gpt-oss draft turned the answer into a product list. The merge kept the reviewer's model-name corrections but not the verdict problem, and recommended shaved sides with a buzzed top, the reverse of what suits crown balding.
great_answer_would: Pick one: a #1-#2 buzz all over with your own clippers every 1-2 weeks, or a clean shave if you will keep it up every 2-3 days. Say why the horseshoe loses and add beard and scalp sunscreen, in under 150 words.
notes: It never tells the asker to drop the long sides or compares the three options he named on looks, and it gives no clipper guard numbers or sunscreen. Four product pitches dominate an answer to a style question.

hallucinations.claim: "The five proven strategies from TaskUp show that a single, repeated agreement works better than repeated nagging"
hallucinations.why: TaskUp is a productivity-app blog about nagging, not evidence about quitting support. Calling it 'proven' is an overclaim.

hallucinations.claim: "Let family members view your progress through the program's shared dashboard"
hallucinations.why: The reviewer flagged that the source does not mention a progress tracker. A shared family dashboard for EX is an invented feature.

hallucinations.claim: "It can raise the odds of quitting by up to 40 %"
hallucinations.why: Truth Initiative's own marketing figure, passed on uncritically; traceable to source [7] but self-reported.

what_went_wrong: The draft drew on generic anti-nagging blogs (TaskUp, Palme School) instead of smokefree.gov's guide for supporters. The merge padded it to eight steps, and two of them (a violation log, deflecting 'try chewing gum') run against the ask and against the evidence that NRT doubles quit rates.
great_answer_would: Hand him a short script to say to his family (don't ask daily; snappiness is withdrawal; distract me; no lecture if I slip), the day 3-7 peak and 2-4 week timeline, a check-in cadence he chooses, and the aids: patch plus gum or lozenge, varenicline, 1-800-QUIT-NOW.
notes: The weekly check-in buddy is a reasonable cadence idea and some scripted phrases are useful. Missing: withdrawal timeline, NRT, varenicline and the quitline. A 'log of violations' is surveillance, the opposite of what he asked for. At about 2,800 chars with a closing recap it is far over the ~200-word target. The EX Program by Truth Initiative with Mayo Clinic is real.
